chapter: Alma Hightower and other women musicians
title: Hightower on piano and in his first Los Angeles band
summary: Howard says she played piano a little and sat in his first band, which played dances around 1906.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: One of our What about at the park? Did she play piano that you know of?
Pretty good. She didn't play too much piano, but she played.
Very good. She wan't a slap-bang player, she just played a little bit, you know.
Uh-huh. Anything else about that? Am I kicking things?
I think we need to check (inaudible)--
I think, Mr. Howard, you mentioned that Miss Hightower worked in your band at some point? Is that what you said a few minutes ago?
Yeah, she came to work out there. In my band. I played--she didn't play many, not pieces, you know.
And that was which band of yours? Was that when you had the "Quality Serenaders" or was that before?
That was when I was first gettin' started playin'. And all I could play was with the musicians, you know.
They came out there, and we did pretty good, too.
So that would've been, do you know about what year?
And that was your first band in Los Angeles? The first one that you led?
Yeah. The first one that I had. It was pretty good.
Where would you work? Did you play dances? Or what kind of jobs did the band work?
She didn't do much of that because there wan't too much she would do, (unintelligible) playin', you know.
She'd get in there, get to playin'. in there--boy, I'm tellin' you. I saved the picture to show you. Can you take this down for a minute?
